title: "NGS library preparation"
title-block-banner: false
---

How to turn DNA or RNA into a molecule a sequencer can read — and how to design a new way of
doing it when no existing protocol fits.

Self-published course material by Johan Henriksson. It is written for late MSc and PhD
students, and it is self-paced: take the parts you need, in the order you need them. There is
no programming in this course. Exercises are design problems, quizzes and enzyme-selection
tasks, with collapsible **Hint** and **Solution** callouts.

The companion to this course is [NGS 101](https://henriksson-lab.github.io/NGS_101/), a
base-by-base reference for about 840 published library chemistries. Protocols named here link
to their page there.

## How the course is built

The course is organised around **blocks**: the steps a protocol is assembled from. Part B
teaches the blocks one at a time. Part C takes real protocols apart and shows which blocks
they are made of, and why two protocols answering the same question differ. Part D is a
reference indexed by the *problem* rather than by the step, and Part E is about judging
whether a library worked and designing one of your own.

If you are here to run an established protocol, read Parts A and E, then the Part C unit for
your assay. If you are here to design something new, the whole course is the argument.

## Part A — Foundations: what the sequencer needs

**[Nucleic acids as a building material](nucleic-acids/lec.qmd)** — strand polarity and end
states, what a ligase actually requires, hybridisation and Tm, degenerate bases, oligo
modifications, how RNA differs.
[Readings](nucleic-acids/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](nucleic-acids/exercise.qmd)

**How sequencers read DNA** — clustering and sequencing by synthesis, the four reads and
their order, i5 orientation, insert size versus read length, index hopping and base
diversity; then MGI, AVITI, Ultima, PacBio and Nanopore, and what each asks of a library.
[Illumina](sequencers/lec.qmd) · [Other platforms](sequencers/lec-platforms.qmd) ·
[Readings](sequencers/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](sequencers/exercise.qmd)

**[Anatomy of a library molecule](library-molecule/lec.qmd)** — P5 to P7 part by part, Y
adapters versus Nextera, full versus truncated adapters, where a barcode or UMI can sit, and
what fails to cluster at all.
[Readings](library-molecule/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](library-molecule/exercise.qmd)

## Part B — Building blocks

The heart of the course, and the most technical part. Each unit covers what the step does to
the molecule, the enzymes and oligos it needs, what it requires of the ends, how it fails,
and the tricks practitioners use.

**The enzyme toolbox** — polymerases along the axes vendor selection charts actually compare,
reverse transcriptases and template switching, ligases and the end states they demand,
kinases and phosphatases, nucleases, transposases and modifying enzymes. Throughout: how to
justify an enzyme choice from a datasheet.
[Polymerases and RTs](enzymes/lec.qmd) · [Ligases, kinases, phosphatases](enzymes/lec-ligases.qmd) ·
[Nucleases](enzymes/lec-nucleases.qmd) · [Transposases and modifying enzymes](enzymes/lec-transposases.qmd) ·
[Readings](enzymes/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](enzymes/exercise.qmd)

**[Attaching a handle — the five ways](handles/lec.qmd)** — the central idea of the course:
there are only a few ways to put a known sequence onto an unknown molecule. Ligation, RNA
ligation, primer tails, transposition, template switching.
[Readings](handles/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](handles/exercise.qmd)

**[End chemistry](end-chemistry/lec.qmd)** — 5′-P versus 5′-OH, blocked 3′ ends, overhangs,
nicks and gaps; end repair, dA-tailing, fill-in; controlling which ends are allowed to ligate.
[Readings](end-chemistry/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](end-chemistry/exercise.qmd)

**[Fragmentation and size control](fragmentation/lec.qmd)** — acoustic, enzymatic,
tagmentation, restriction, MNase; size targets set by the sequencer; why fragmenting before
or after the key chemistry changes the answer.
[Readings](fragmentation/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](fragmentation/exercise.qmd)

**[Amplification](amplification/lec.qmd)** — PCR bias, duplicates and cycle number;
PCR-free; linear amplification and IVT; RCA, MDA and PTA; suppressing adapter dimers.
[Readings](amplification/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](amplification/exercise.qmd)

**[Selection — keeping what you want](selection/lec.qmd)** — affinity, hybridisation capture,
depletion with RNase H or Cas9, enzymatic and physical selection, and selecting by end
structure rather than by sequence.
[Readings](selection/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](selection/exercise.qmd)

**[Barcodes, UMIs and where information lives](barcodes-umis/lec.qmd)** — index design, cell
barcodes, where a UMI may be added and why never in PCR, and budgeting the read structure.
[Readings](barcodes-umis/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](barcodes-umis/exercise.qmd)

**[Converting chemistry into sequence](chemistry-to-sequence/lec.qmd)** — the trick that makes
anything measurable: turn a property into a base change, an end, or a ligation event.
[Readings](chemistry-to-sequence/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](chemistry-to-sequence/exercise.qmd)

**[Compartments](compartments/lec.qmd)** — keeping the molecules of one cell together: wells,
droplets, nuclei, hydrogels, split-and-pool; Poisson loading, doublets and collisions.
[Readings](compartments/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](compartments/exercise.qmd)

## Part C — Use cases: blocks assembled into protocols

Each unit takes a biological question, derives the protocol from the blocks above, then reads
real protocols from the collection and asks why they differ.

**[Genomic DNA](genomic-dna/lec.qmd)** — shotgun and PCR-free, degraded and ancient DNA, low
input, single-cell whole-genome amplification; coverage uniformity and GC bias.
[Readings](genomic-dna/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](genomic-dna/exercise.qmd)

**RNA** — choosing by RNA class; rRNA depletion, RT priming, second-strand synthesis, dUTP
strandedness; tag counting versus full length; small RNA and low input.
[mRNA and total RNA](rna/lec.qmd) · [Small RNA, tag protocols, low input](rna/lec-small-rna.qmd) ·
[Readings](rna/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](rna/exercise.qmd)

**[Targeted sequencing](targeted/lec.qmd)** — amplicons and tiled panels, hybrid capture,
MIPs and padlocks, Cas9-guided enrichment, reduced representation; why rare-variant detection
forces UMIs or duplex tags.
[Readings](targeted/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](targeted/exercise.qmd)

**[Chromatin and protein–DNA](chromatin/lec.qmd)** — accessibility and binding; crosslinking
and its reversal; the tethered-enzyme idea (pA-MNase, pA-Tn5) treated as a block.
[Readings](chromatin/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](chromatin/exercise.qmd)

**[Three-dimensional genome and contacts](3d-genome/lec.qmd)** — proximity ligation as a
block: crosslink, digest, ligate, pull down the junction; 3C through Micro-C; ligation-free
approaches.
[Readings](3d-genome/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](3d-genome/exercise.qmd)

**Modifications, damage and dynamics** — bisulfite and its successors, break mapping,
replication timing; m6A, the CLIP family, metabolic labelling, nascent RNA and TSS mapping.
[DNA](modifications/lec.qmd) · [RNA](modifications/lec-rna.qmd) ·
[Readings](modifications/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](modifications/exercise.qmd)

**Single cells** — the same blocks, but every molecule must carry a compartment barcode.
Plates, droplets and microwells; combinatorial indexing; multimodal assays.
[Plates, droplets, microwells](single-cell/lec.qmd) ·
[Combinatorial indexing and multimodal](single-cell/lec-combinatorial.qmd) ·
[Readings](single-cell/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](single-cell/exercise.qmd)

**[Spatial](spatial/lec.qmd)** — array capture, microfluidic barcoding, region selection and
in situ sequencing; fixation and permeabilisation as the limiting chemistry.
[Readings](spatial/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](spatial/exercise.qmd)

**Pooled screens and synthetic libraries** — oligo pools, pooled cloning, lentiviral
integration; then the readout treated as a library-prep problem in its own right.
[Building the library](screens/lec.qmd) · [Reading it out](screens/lec-readout.qmd) ·
[Readings](screens/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](screens/exercise.qmd)

**[Long reads](long-reads/lec.qmd)** — handling HMW DNA and what shears it; PacBio SMRTbell
and Iso-Seq; ONT ligation, rapid, ultra-long and direct RNA; Cas9 enrichment and adaptive
sampling.
[Readings](long-reads/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](long-reads/exercise.qmd)

## Part D — The trick catalogue

Indexed by the problem rather than by the step. Each entry gives the problem, the trick, the
molecular reason it works, and protocols that use it. These can be read in any order, and
this is the part to come back to while at the bench.
[Ligation, clean-up, handles and the read](tricks/lec.qmd) ·
[Counting, low input, compartments and bases](tricks/lec-more.qmd) ·
[Readings](tricks/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](tricks/exercise.qmd)

## Part E — Quality control and designing your own

**[Cleanup, quantification and QC](qc/lec.qmd)** — how an SPRI ratio sets the cut-off; what
Qubit, qPCR and a fragment analyser each actually measure; pooling, denaturing and loading;
reading a trace for adapter dimers and over-amplification.
[Readings](qc/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](qc/exercise.qmd)

**[Design patterns, failure modes and the capstone](design/lec.qmd)** — reading a protocol as
a sequence of blocks and drawing the construct after every step; failure signatures and the
controls that distinguish them; then design a library prep of your own and compare it with
the closest protocol in the collection.
[Readings](design/readings.qmd) · [Exercise](design/exercise.qmd)
